title: Palindromic substrings → longest palindrome
label: ag-single
statement: Return the **number of palindromic substrings** of `s`. Substrings at different positions count separately even if they read the same.
provenance: Named as the medium-to-hard question in a 2025 Agoda HackerRank OA report ("palindromic substrings — solved it but couldn't optimise"). One report. Stage 2 is the standard companion problem.

sources.name: LeetCode Discuss — Agoda Online Assessment, Senior Software Engineer

clarify: Do identical substrings at different positions count separately? (Yes.)
How long can s be? (Thousands — O(n³) is too slow.)

stages.title: Count them
stages.say: How many palindromic substrings does this string have?
testNames: in … ms (< 1500 — needs O(n^2), not O(n^3))

stages.title: The longest one
stages.say: Same centres, different question: return the longest palindromic substring.
stages.require: Add `Palindromes.Longest(s)`; the leftmost if several share the maximum length.

prompts.label: Check my design — no code
prompts.text: I believe every palindrome has a centre — a character or the gap between two — so expanding from each of the 2n−1 centres counts all of them in O(n²) time and O(1) space, versus O(n³) for checking every substring. Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?

prompts.label: Review, do not rewrite

prompts.label: Race conditions
prompts.text: Now review this implementation for race conditions if multiple threads call CountSubstrings concurrently. For each race, give the interleaving that breaks it. Then name the smallest synchronization boundary that preserves correctness. Do not write code yet.

prompts.label: Tests that expose bugs
prompts.text: Suggest tests that could expose bugs in my implementation: boundaries, duplicates, empty and invalid input, and concurrency where it applies. For each, say why the expected value is correct.

prompts.label: Complexity check
prompts.text: What is the time and space complexity of each public method as written? Do not claim a bound unless every step achieves it.

prompts.label: Requirement change
prompts.text: The requirement changed: Add Palindromes.Longest(s); the leftmost if several share the maximum length. List which members need to change and which do not, before writing any code.

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: Return the **number of palindromic substrings** of `s`. Substrings at different positions count separately even if they read the same.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Do identical substrings at different positions count separately? (Yes.)
- Single characters count? (Yes.)
- How long can s be? (Thousands — O(n³) is too slow.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: Instead of testing each substring (n² of them, each O(n)), grow palindromes outward from their centres; every successful expansion is one more palindrome, so the count falls out for free.

learn.title: 4 · Approach

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- O(n³) brute force — the report says it was the optimisation that failed.
- Forgetting even-length centres.
- int overflow for the count on long uniform strings (use long).
- Manacher's algorithm attempted under time pressure when O(n²) is accepted.
